title: Archive-first benchmark hashstore and investigation canvas for fast anomaly resolution
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build an append-only, content-addressed benchmark result store (hashstore) optimized for deduplication and fast snapshot diffs, plus a linked Investigation Canvas UI that surfaces correlated signals (tokens/sec, p95, mem/gpu usage, queue depth) to speed up anomaly triage. Goal: reduce mean time to root cause (MTTR) for perf regressions by enabling 1-click cohort replay, side-by-side metric alignment, and origin fingerprinting.
background: Current benchmark workflows store dense JSON blobs per run with substantial duplication across minor config changes. Triage requires manual aggregation of runs, handcrafted queries, and repeated playbacks. Recent regressions took >48h to resolve due to noisy signals and missing run lineage. We need high-cardinality indexing, cheap diffs, and a UI that guides an engineer through correlation lanes and likely root causes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hashstore accepts existing benchmark run format and deduplicates identical payloads by content hash. 2) Query API returns diff summary between two snapshots in <1s for typical run sizes. 3) Investigation Canvas shows aligned p95/tokens/sec/time-series, highlights top-correlated signals, and allows cohort replay trigger to ABI-compatible harness. 4) End-to-end demo with sample regression completes within cycle and PR merged.
technical_design_notes:
- Store blobs in S3-like object store keyed by content-hash (sha256), with a small Postgres index mapping run_id -> list of content-hash parts and metadata.
- Break benchmark results into normalized shards: metrics, config, model-metadata, traces. Each shard hashed separately to maximize dedupe.
- Precompute lightweight fingerprints: latency-quantile vector (p50,p90,p95,p99), tokens_per_sec, gpu_utilization_summary. These sit in timeseries index (Influx/TSDB) for fast retrieval.
- Diff engine computes per-metric delta and produces a normalized human-readable checklist of changed fields. Use reservoir sampling for traces to keep diff bounded.
- Investigation Canvas: React app with lanes for metrics, traces, env/config diffs, related PRs. Correlation engine runs quick Pearson + rank-correlation over aligned windows and surfaces top 3 candidate signals.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives:
- Full event sourcing with Kafka would provide richer lineage but increases operational burden; chosen store+index approach minimizes infra changes.
- Could use a commercial time-series DB for correlation, but we will prototype with our existing TSDB to reduce dependencies.
- Deduping at shard-level increases complexity but gives largest storage savings vs whole-blob dedupe.
implementation_plan: 1) Data sharding + hashing library (Diego) - 3d. 2) Index schema + migration script (Sujata) - 2d. 3) Diff engine + fingerprints (backend) - 4d. 4) Canvas UI prototype + correlation hooks (frontend) - 5d. 5) Integrate cohort replay endpoint with harness (runtime) - 2d. 6) End-to-end e2e tests and demo - 3d.
rollout_plan: - Feature-flagged behind bench_hashstore. Roll out to staging first, run 2 weeks of mirror ingest. If no data loss/corruption, enable on a single customer sandbox and run a simulated regression exercise. Gradual enablement across testbeds.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for hashing and dedupe.
- Integration test that ingests 1000 synthetic runs and verifies index size reductions and diff latencies.
- End-to-end triage scenario: introduce controlled latency regression and verify Investigation Canvas surfaces the GPU sched delay as top correlate.
- Load test ingest path at 200 rps sustained.
migration_notes: Backfill existing archive by chunking old blobs into shards and computing hashes. Backfill can run offline; plan: run in parallel with normal ingest and mark runs as migrated when complete. Provide migration progress metrics in console.
open_risks:
- Hash collisions extremely unlikely but handle with double-check on full content equality; need careful rollbacks if index misaligns.
- Correlation false-positives: Canvas must mark suggestions as heuristics and not authoritative.
- Storage cost shift: more small objects could increase PUT costs; need batching/aggregation optimization.
next_steps: Finish hashing library and unit tests
Wire up timeseries fingerprints to TSDB ingest path
Sketch initial Canvas lanes and wire correlation API
